findings.title: UPDATE statement missing WHERE clause extends every session's expiry
findings.description: The SQL `UPDATE tokens SET expires_at = ?` has no WHERE clause, so refreshing one token extends the expires_at of every token row in the table for every user, not just the token being refreshed. This is both a correctness bug and a security issue: it silently prolongs the sessions of all other logged-in users (including ones that should have expired), which could let stale or attacker-obtained tokens remain valid indefinitely.

findings.title: refresh_token allows unbounded sliding expiry
findings.description: authenticate() only checks that the token is not yet expired, so refresh_token() lets a client extend a session indefinitely as long as it refreshes before each expiry, with no absolute session lifetime cap. A stolen token could be kept alive forever by an attacker who refreshes it periodically.

findings.title: Test does not verify refresh behavior or catch the missing WHERE clause bug
findings.description: test_refresh_token only asserts that refresh_token returns the same token string; it never checks that expires_at was actually updated for that token, and critically never checks that other users' tokens are unaffected. This test would pass even with the UPDATE-all-rows bug, so it fails to catch a critical defect. It also doesn't test refreshing an expired or invalid token.
